description: Correlated EXISTS subqueries nested inside one another, where an inner subquery correlates to the MIDDLE query rather than to the outermost one. t1 {1,2,3,4} / t2 {1,2,3} / t3 {1,2} / t4 {1}: one level of EXISTS keeps 1,2,3; two levels keep 1,2 (3 survives the t2 test but has no t3 partner); three levels keep only 1. The correlation chain is what is under test - t1.i = t2.i in the middle and t2.i = t3.i in the innermost - so a flattening that lost the middle reference would answer with more rows. Converted 1:1 from query/NestedCorrelatedQueryTest (now retired); the Java asserted row COUNTS and read the first rows by index, so the converted tests pin the whole ordered row set, and the class's manual-check test - which only LOGGED each table's contents before re-running the same query - asserts those contents.

steps.sql: SELECT * FROM t1 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t2 WHERE t1.i = t2.i AND EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t3 WHERE t2.i = t3.i)) ORDER BY i
SELECT * FROM t1 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t2 WHERE t1.i = t2.i) ORDER BY i
SELECT * FROM t1 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t2 WHERE t1.i = t2.i AND EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t3 WHERE t2.i = t3.i AND EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t4 WHERE t3.i = t4.i))) ORDER BY i
SELECT * FROM t1 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t2 WHERE t1.i = t2.i AND EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t3 WHERE t2.i = t3.i)) ORDER BY i
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT * FROM t1 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t2 WHERE t1.i = t2.i AND EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t3 WHERE t2.i = t3.i)) ORDER BY i)
SELECT i FROM t1 ORDER BY i
SELECT i FROM t2 ORDER BY i
SELECT i FROM t3 ORDER BY i
SELECT * FROM t1 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t2 WHERE t1.i = t2.i AND EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t3 WHERE t2.i = t3.i)) ORDER BY i
